approaches.hypothesis: The bug occurs because paths like './some/path', 'some/path', and 'some//path' are treated as different when checking against ignore-path patterns, even though they refer to the same location. Normalizing the path before the check would make the pattern matching consistent. This would be falsified if the issue persists after normalization or if the problem lies elsewhere in the path handling logic.
approaches.measurement: Applied the upstream fix: added `element = os.path.normpath(element)` after line 54 (after `def _is_ignored_file(...) -> bool:` function signature) in pylint/lint/expand_modules.py, verified against the diff from PR #7080 which shows the exact change made.
approaches.name: normpath-before-ignore-check
approaches.source: GitHub issue #6964 (filed Jun 16, 2022) and PR #7080 (merged Jun 28, 2022) which fixed this exact bug in pylint 2.14.4. The fix added `element = os.path.normpath(element)` at the start of the `_is_ignored_file()` function in `pylint/lint/expand_modules.py`. The PR merged into maintenance/2.14.x branch and was included in pylint 2.14.4 release. URL: https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint/pull/7080
approaches.summary: Normalize file paths using os.path.normpath() before checking against ignore-paths patterns
